note: The agent control plane. ABSENT in the no-agents profile (PRD decision 40.6) — these rows and the routes that carry them are simply not there, so a request 404s. The edge registers them from this file: `forward` maps /agent/<path> onto agent-api's /api/<path>, every row but the catch-all is a route of its own (`stream` relays server-sent events), `delegation` admits a worker's own delegation token — on the friction report its harness files, and nowhere else — and `mcp_reentry` admits it on the MCP's re-entry: one row per route a tool in mcp.tools.v1.json calls, and no other. `verbs` rows are agent-api's own verbs behind the forward, by public path, carrying a policy the catch-all cannot: `person` — the verb needs a person in the loop, and agent-api refuses a worker dispatched without one (`control_plane/route_policy.py`). The edge does not register them. `shared` (D3, default-deny for shared tokens, 0.13.4) is on EVERY row and verb: may a worker whose turn other people read (a room's or a shared chat's delegation, `scope.shared`) reach the route — `allow` or `refuse`. agent-api enforces it once, from the signed delegation, on the route a request matched (`control_plane/route_policy.py` SHARED_GATE); a route this app serves that no row or verb declares is refused to a shared token and fails the boot and CI (`tests/test_shared_routes.py`). Every verb agent-api serves under the forward has a row here, `person: false` where no person is needed. The MCP edge shows a shared caller only tools whose route says `allow`.
